questions.q: A company must copy 200 TB from an on-premises NFS server to S3 over Direct Connect and keep the copy in sync afterwards, with integrity checks. Which service fits best?

options.t: `aws s3 sync` run by cron
options.why: Wrong: it works but is slower, single-path, and has no managed retries, verification or monitoring.

options.t: AWS DMS
options.why: Wrong: DMS migrates databases, not file shares.

options.t: AWS DataSync with an agent and a scheduled task
options.why: Right: an agent reads NFS, the task transfers only changed data after the first run and verifies integrity.

options.t: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)
options.why: Wrong: MGN migrates whole servers, not file data.

questions.explain: Online, recurring, verified file transfer from NFS/SMB to AWS is DataSync.
questions.remember: Online bulk or recurring file/object transfer into S3, EFS or FSx, with integrity checks → DataSync (agent for on-premises sources).
variants: Database migration → DMS.
Whole server migration → MGN.
SFTP/FTPS partners uploading → Transfer Family.
Poor or no network → Snow Family or Data Transfer Terminal.

questions.q: A team must copy a bucket in account A to a bucket in account B (both S3) using DataSync. They want the least operational effort. What is needed?

options.t: An EC2-hosted agent in each account
options.why: Wrong: an agent is not required when S3 is one side of a cross-account transfer.

options.t: A Direct Connect link between the accounts
options.why: Wrong: S3 traffic does not need Direct Connect and it is not part of DataSync requirements.

options.t: A VMware agent on-premises
options.why: Wrong: nothing on-premises is involved.

options.t: No agent; create locations and a task
options.why: Right: S3 to other AWS storage across accounts needs no agent.

questions.explain: Agents are needed for on-premises sources, not for S3 to AWS storage.
questions.remember: No agent for AWS storage to AWS storage in one account, S3 to other AWS storage cross-account, or S3 to other-cloud object storage. Agent for on-premises sources.
variants: Source is on-premises NFS → agent needed.
EFS/FSx to another cloud → agent needed.
Azure Blob to S3 → no agent.
Both sides EFS/FSx in different accounts → may need an agent.

questions.q: A DataSync task copies hundreds of millions of objects to S3 and Basic mode keeps hitting the item quota. What should the team do?

options.t: Switch the existing task to Enhanced mode
options.why: Wrong: task mode cannot be changed after creation.

options.t: Create the task in Enhanced mode
options.why: Right: Enhanced mode lists, prepares, transfers and verifies in parallel and has virtually unlimited objects per execution.

options.t: Add more agents to the location
options.why: Wrong: agents add throughput but do not remove the Basic mode quota (25 to 50 million).

options.t: Raise the bandwidth limit
options.why: Wrong: the limit throttles speed; it does not change item quotas.

questions.explain: Enhanced mode removes the practical item limit; mode is fixed at creation.
questions.remember: Very many objects → Enhanced mode (create a new task, mode cannot change). Basic mode has 25 to 50 million item quotas, or split with filters.
variants: Destination is FSx for Windows File Server → Basic mode.
You want to avoid creating a new task → split the data by prefix with filters in Basic mode.
Need full point-in-time verification → Basic mode only.

questions.q: A DataSync task writes data straight into the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class. Which verification setting is correct?

options.t: Disable CloudWatch Logs
options.why: Wrong: logging does not control verification.

options.t: Verify all data in Enhanced mode
options.why: Wrong: Enhanced mode only verifies transferred data, and Glacier classes need the same.

options.t: `ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED`
options.why: Right: it checks only transferred data and is required for Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive.

options.t: `POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT`
options.why: Wrong: full comparison is not supported for Glacier classes.

questions.remember: Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive destination → set the storage class on the task and use ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED.
variants: Want a full compare at the end → POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT (Basic mode, not Glacier).
Want checks only during transfer → NONE.
Archived objects at the source → restore them first or they are skipped.

questions.q: A nightly DataSync copy shares a 1 Gbps link with production traffic. Which task option protects production?

options.t: Enable task reports
options.why: Wrong: reports describe results only.

options.t: Set a bandwidth limit on the task
options.why: Right: it throttles bytes per second for each task execution.

options.t: Use include/exclude filters
options.why: Wrong: filters choose files, they do not control speed.

options.t: Add up to 4 agents to the location
options.why: Wrong: more agents increase throughput and make congestion worse.

questions.remember: Link shared with production → bandwidth limit on the task. Need only certain files → filters or a manifest.
variants: Move an exact list of files → manifest.
Skip *.tmp files → exclude filter.
Need faster transfer → more agents or Enhanced mode.

questions.q: A company needs an on-premises share synced to S3 every 15 minutes with DataSync scheduling. What is the issue?

options.t: Only Enhanced mode supports sub-hour schedules
options.why: Wrong: the minimum applies to all modes.

options.t: Schedules require Lambda
options.why: Wrong: schedules are built in using EventBridge-style expressions.

options.t: The minimum schedule interval is 1 hour, so use another approach for faster sync
options.why: Right: DataSync schedules accept cron or rate expressions with a 1-hour minimum.

options.t: It works with a rate of 15 minutes
options.why: Wrong: the minimum is 1 hour.

questions.remember: DataSync scheduled tasks run at most hourly. Faster flows → File Gateway, Transfer Family or S3 Replication; or start tasks from EventBridge/API.
variants: Hourly or slower → built-in task schedule.
S3 to S3 continuous → S3 Replication.
Need to pause schedule → set it DISABLED.

questions.q: A security team requires DataSync agent traffic to never cross the public internet. What should be used?

options.t: The public endpoint with TLS
options.why: Wrong: TLS encrypts the traffic but it still uses the public internet.

options.t: A bandwidth limit
options.why: Wrong: it only throttles speed.

options.t: A FIPS endpoint
options.why: Wrong: FIPS is for compliance, not private routing.

options.t: A VPC interface endpoint (PrivateLink) for DataSync
options.why: Right: agent to service traffic stays on private connectivity.

questions.remember: Agent traffic must stay off the internet → VPC (PrivateLink) endpoint. FIPS endpoint → compliance requirement. All data is TLS-encrypted in transit anyway.
variants: Compliance needs FIPS 140 endpoints → FIPS endpoint.
Encryption in transit only → already TLS by default.
SMB credentials storage → Secrets Manager.

questions.q: A DataSync task to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket fails with access denied, although the bucket policy allows the DataSync role. What is the likely fix?

options.t: Raise the task quota
options.why: Wrong: quotas do not cause access denied.

options.t: Grant the S3 location IAM role the needed KMS permissions
options.why: Right: for SSE-KMS buckets the role DataSync assumes also needs KMS access.

options.t: Add a second agent
options.why: Wrong: S3 access uses the IAM role, not agents.

options.t: Switch the task to Basic mode
options.why: Wrong: mode does not affect KMS permissions.

questions.explain: SSE-KMS bucket needs KMS permissions on the DataSync role.
questions.remember: DataSync reaches S3 through an IAM role trusted by datasync.amazonaws.com; for SSE-KMS buckets that role also needs KMS permissions. Scope it to the bucket/prefix.
variants: NFS permission denied → check export, ACLs and root squash.
Agent offline → check network, VM, endpoint.
Cross-account → bucket policy plus role.
